newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenian leader quells protests with show of force.
newsitem.headline: Armenian leader quells protests with show of force.

text.p: Armenian President Levon Ter-Petrosyan has moved troops and armoured vehicles into the capital Yerevan and detained political opponents following disputed election results and violence outside parliament.

An interior ministry spokesman told Reuters on Thursday that six opposition members of parliament had been detained after the chamber, in which Ter-Petrosyan's ruling bloc dominate, voted to allow prosecutors to press charges against them.
Several were punched repeatedly by the deputies.
"Vazgen Manukyan is being sought," the spokesman said by telephone, referring to the opposition leader who says he won Sunday's presidential election.
But Radio Liberty correspondent Genel Malbadyan said he had seen Manukyan in a hallway of the parliament just before Thursday's session began.

He said the former prime minister, who was surrounded by about 10 armed security force members, refused to enter the hall. The report could not be confirmed and Manukyan's present whereabouts were not known.
As a presidential candidate, Manukyan has special immunity from arrest until Sunday, Central Electoral Commission chief Khachik Bezirjyan told Reuters.
Security forces earlier in the day sealed off Manukyan's National Democratic Union headquarters.

The unofficial results in the presidential vote gave Ter-Petrosyan 52 percent of the vote to 41 percent for Manukyan. Ter-Petrosyan needed 50 percent of the vote to avoid a second-round runoff with the former prime minister.
But international observers saw numerous cases of outright fraud being committed by Ter-Petrosyan officials both in the voting and counting process.

Ter-Petrosyan, 50, has led this small Caucasus country of 3.5 million since independence in 1991, a period marked by hardship caused largely by confrontation with neighbouring Azerbaijan over the disputed enclave of Nagorno-Karabakh.
Conditions have eased in recent months but Armenia has suffered many winters of power cuts and shortages.
The decision to bring in troops followed violent clashes on Wednesday night between riot troops and thousands of Manukyan's supporters who accuse Ter-Petrosyan of rigging the vote.
Some protesters charged into the parliament building and beat the speaker and vice-speaker. Riot troops regained control after a nearly hour-long battle in front of the legislature.
An aide to Ter-Petrosyan told Reuters one soldier and one protester had been killed in the clashes and dozens were hurt.
Light tanks belching blue smoke sped along Yerevan streets while several thousand troops with Kalashnikov automatic rifles sealed off the centre.
Reporters saw soldiers dispersing small groups gathering in a square where Manukyan's supporters used to rally. At least two people were beaten and taken away.
Ter-Petrosyan banned rallies and demonstrations in an early morning TV address, calling opposition politicians "mentally ill" people who had tried to stage a coup.
